preconditions.description: The number of test cases is between 1 and 50,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= k <= n <= 100000 for n, k in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is the number of nodes (2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5), and k is the maximum allowed edges to delete (2 ≤ k ≤ n).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= 1000000000 for a in test_cases for a_i in a)
preconditions.description: Each node value a_i is between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, _, _, edges in test_cases)
preconditions.description: The input graph is a tree with exactly n-1 edges.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u_i <= n and 1 <= v_i <= n and u_i != v_i for n, _, _, edges in test_cases for u_i, v_i in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes within the valid range.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'YES' if exists(1 <= m <= k - 1 and all(xor_component == target_xor for xor_component in xor_components)) else stdout == 'NO'
postconditions.description: The output is 'YES' if there exists a way to delete between 1 and k-1 edges such that the XOR of node values in every connected component is the same. Otherwise, output 'NO'. Here, xor_components is the list of XORs of node values in each connected component after deletion, and target_xor is the common XOR value.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout in ['YES', 'NO', 'yes', 'no', 'Yes', 'No'] for stdout in outputs)
postconditions.description: The output for each test case is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive).
